narr: As the remnants of what was once Hurricane Kay off the coast of southern California continued to bring beneficial tropical moisture into New Mexico on September 12, 2022, it led to another day of scattered showers and thunderstorms across the area. While heavy rainfall was observed with these thunderstorms along with slow storm motions, flash flooding reports were not received with the exception of the McBride burn scar. A brief thunderstorm developed over the burn area, and while rainfall totals were generally observed to be around or less than 0.10, the emergency manager reported that very localized heavy rainfall fell right over Gavilan Ridge. Unfortunately, this water then flowed directly onto Gavilan Canyon Road which has been significantly impacted this monsoon season.
ev: Localized heavy rainfall on Gavilan Ridge flowed downhill onto the McBride burn scar which caused flash flooding along Gavilan Canyon Road from Janet Drive northward to Airplane Canyon. Burn scar flash flooding resulted in rock and mud debris along the roadway. Damages are estimated.
